picks.title: Learning functions of Hamiltonians with Hamiltonian Fourier features
picks.abstract: We propose a quantum machine learning task that is provably easy for quantum computers and hard for classical ones. The task involves predicting quantities of the form T r [ f ( H ) ρ ] , where f is an unknown function, given descriptions of H and ρ . Using a Fourier-based feature map of Hamiltonians and linear regression, we theoretically establish the learnability of the task and implement it on a superconducting device using up to 72 qubits. This work provides a machine learning task with practical relevance, provable quantum easiness, and near-term feasibility.

picks.title: Floquet Engineering of a Quasiequilibrium Superradiant Phase Transition in Landau Polaritons
picks.abstract: Superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs), characterized by photon condensation and macroscopic matter polarization, are forbidden in equilibrium for homogeneous fields by no-go theorems. Here, we show that Floquet driving can circumvent this constraint in a Landau polariton system consisting of a two-dimensional electron gas coupled to a terahertz cavity in a DC magnetic field. An off-resonant AC magnetic field modulates the cyclotron frequency and light-matter coupling strength while leaving the diamagnetic term unchanged, generating an additional DC coupling contribution. This drives the system across a critical threshold into a superradiant phase, characterized by photon condensation and Landau-level polarization in the ground state of the Floquet Hamiltonian. This quasiequilibrium approach offers a route to SRPTs distinct from driven-dissipative schemes.

picks.title: A JWST/NIRSpec Catalog of Low-mass Candidates toward NGC 2024 from Multicomponent Spectral Modeling
picks.abstract: Young low-mass objects in crowded, highly obscured star-forming regions are difficult to characterize. Deriving reliable physical parameters requires separating photospheric emission from complex extinction and circumstellar emission. We apply a multicomponent spectral-modeling framework to JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra toward NGC 2024, obtaining adopted fits for 78 sources. The framework incorporates atmospheric models, dust and ice opacities, and optional thermal emission. Most spectra favor additional large-H 2 O-ice opacity over the baseline small-grain model, while a smaller subset requires additional gray opacity, potentially arising from large refractory grains. Some spectra also require a thermal component to reproduce the long-wavelength continuum. The parameters inferred with this framework, together with the NGC 2024 distance, yield radii and bolometric luminosities. Comparison with evolutionary models for young low-mass and substellar objects provides mass estimates and identifies 46 candidate members, 27 sources classified as background, and 5 uncertain sources. Candidate members show lower fitted surface gravities than likely background stars. Of the candidate members, 23 lie above the youngest available isochrones, plausibly reflecting the cluster’s youth and uncertainties in model initial conditions. The resulting catalog provides a uniform characterization of the NGC 2024 sample and establishes a framework for treating complex extinction and circumstellar emission in JWST spectra of other obscured star-forming regions.

picks.title: The Luminosity Function and Isotropic Energy Function of Long Gamma-Ray Bursts in the Comoving Frame
picks.abstract: We study the comoving-frame properties of 77 long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with initial Lorentz factor (Γ 0 ) estimates, including parameter distributions, spectral-energy correlations, luminosity functions, and isotropic energy functions. Specifically, the comoving-frame distributions are significantly narrower than those in the rest frame, while the Amati and Yonetoku relations still exist but become considerably weaker, indicating that relativistic Doppler effects contribute strongly to the observed correlations. Using the Lynden-Bell c − method, we find significant redshift evolution of both luminosity and isotropic energy, with consistent evolution indices within statistical uncertainties in each frame, implying that LGRB duration may not exhibit significant redshift evolution. After de-evolution, the luminosity functions are well described by triple power laws in both frames. In contrast, the isotropic energy function changes from a broken power law in the rest frame to a triple power law in the comoving frame, with much steeper high-energy tails. This indicates that the energy-function shape in previous works is strongly affected by Γ 0 and suggests an effective upper envelope in the comoving-frame energy scale. Overall, our results demonstrate that the Γ 0 correction is essential for revealing the intrinsic properties of LGRBs.

picks.title: Investigation of Cu(II) Binding by Human Calprotectin Reveals an Unusual Fluxional Coordination Environment
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Human calprotectin (CP, S100A8/S100A9 heterooligomer) is a multi-metal sequestering protein that contributes to the innate immune response by starving invading microbial pathogens of essential metal nutrients. Despite the ability of CP to withhold copper from microbial pathogens, its copper coordination chemistry is largely unexplored. Here we elucidate the Cu(II)-binding properties of CP-Ser [S100A8(C42S)/S100A9(C3S) variant] under conditions of high and low Ca(II) and present a working model for how CP sequesters Cu(II). Our biochemical and spectroscopic studies reveal that both the His3Asp and His6 sites bind Cu(II) with Ca(II)-dependent affinity, and Cu(II) binding to both sites is required for Cu(II)-dependent self-association of CP heterodimers to heterotetramers. Moreover, our spectroscopic data demonstrate that Cu(II) binds to the His6 site in a fluxional coordination environment, and that the mode of Cu(II) binding is allosterically modulated by Ca(II) coordination to the EF-hand domains and Cu(II) binding at the His3Asp site. Sequestration of Cu(II) using a fluxional His6 site contrasts with how CP captures other nutrient M(II) (M = Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn) at this site using a static and nearly idealized octahedral binding mode. This study reveals the remarkable ability of a fluxional site to participate in metal sequestration at the host-pathogen interface.

picks.title: Good Practices and Common Pitfalls in the Research and Development of New Electrolytes for Flow Batteries
picks.abstract: Redox flow batteries represent one of the most actively investigated platforms for grid-scale electrochemical energy storage. The rapid expansion of electrolyte chemistries has broadened the field, but has also introduced significant inconsistencies in experimental methods, testing protocols, and reporting practices. This variability impedes interlaboratory comparison and, in some cases, produces misleading assessments of electrolyte performance and stability. This article presents structured, practical guidance for researchers working with novel flow battery electrolytes, organized around four core activities: electrolyte formulation and physicochemical characterization, electroanalytical screening, flow cell assembly and hardware selection, and performance and lifetime evaluation. Key topics include staged characterization of redox-active compounds from dilute cyclic voltammetry through operationally relevant conditions, component selection and compatibility checks, the distinction between symmetric and full cell configurations for performance versus lifetime testing, and the role of potentiostatic cycling protocols in generating reliable capacity fade data. Finally, the reporting of capacity fade is discussed with consideration of the underlying degradation mechanisms. The guidance is condensed into ten practical recommendations, and the article is published as a living document on GitHub, open to continuous community revision and peer review to work toward a community consensus on experimental and reporting practices in our field.

picks.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
picks.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1–3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4–7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse. Single-cell epigenetic analyses reveal a conserved epigenetic signature across patients that may help identify those at increased risk for disease relapse in breast cancer.

picks.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
picks.abstract: Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

picks.title: Functional Fixed Dystonia of the Foot
picks.abstract: A previously healthy 23-year-old woman presented with an 11-month history of foot pain and difficulty walking. Neurologic examination showed the left foot fixed in plantar flexion and inversion (shown in a video).
picks.topic: Deep Brain Stimulation and Movement Disorders

picks.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice
picks.abstract: Study Objectives Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group). Results IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve. Conclusions IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. more.title: Plasma Conductivity from Warm Dense Matter to the Spitzer Limit Using Mean-Force Kinetic Theory
more.abstract: A theoretical model is developed to compute electronic transport coefficients extending from warm and dense to hot and dilute plasma conditions. This kinetic theory-based approach models strong Coulomb correlations by treating collisions using the potential of mean force, electron degeneracy using the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation, and diffraction by computing cross sections quantum mechanically. Hydrodynamic transport coefficients are computed by solving the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation using the Chapman-Enskog method. The result provides a fast and accurate means to compute electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and electrothermal coefficients, including contributions from electron-electron collisions. The model enables accurate calculation of materials properties in many warm dense matter systems, including inertial confinement fusion, stellar evolution, and high energy density plasma experiments.

more.title: Study of K S 0 a 0 ( 980 ) 0 and K ‾ * ( 892 ) 0 η in the D 0 → K S 0 π 0 η decay
more.abstract: We perform an amplitude analysis of the decay D 0 → K S 0 π 0 η and measure its absolute branching fraction to be ( 1.016 ± 0.013 stat. ± 0.014 syst. ) % . The analysis utilizes 20.3 fb − 1 of e + e − collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV with the BESIII detector. We precisely determine ℬ ( D 0 → K S 0 a 0 ( 980 ) 0 , a 0 ( 980 ) 0 → π 0 η ) = ( 9.47 ± 0.36 stat. ± 0.40 syst. ) × 10 − 3 , improving the precision of the world average by a factor of 4.5. Combined with our previous result, these measurements differ from q q ‾ model predictions by an order of magnitude but agree well with tetraquark predictions, strongly supporting the a 0 ( 980 ) as a tetraquark state. Furthermore, the branching fraction of the intermediate process D 0 → K ‾ * ( 892 ) 0 η is determined to be ( 0.70 ± 0.05 stat. ± 0.03 syst. ) % , which is 5 σ smaller than the result measured in D 0 → K − π + η by the Belle experiment. As a result, the magnitudes of the W -exchange and QCD-penguin amplitudes are found to be less than half of their current estimations.

more.title: Emergent self-inhibition governs the landscape of stable states in complex ecosystems
more.abstract: Species-rich ecosystems often exhibit multiple stable states with distinct species compositions. Yet, the factors determining the likelihood of each state’s occurrence remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize and explain the landscape of stable states in the random Generalized Lotka-Volterra (GLV) model, in which multistability is widespread. We focus on the regime of the model where interspecies interactions are predominantly competitive and nearly symmetric. We find that the same pool of species with random initial abundances can result in different stable states, whose likelihoods typically differ by orders of magnitude. A state’s likelihood increases sharply with its total biomass, or inverse self-inhibition. We develop a simplified model to predict and explain this behavior, by coarse-graining ecological interactions so that each stable state behaves as a unit. In this setting, we can accurately predict the entire landscape of stable states using only two macroscopic properties: the biomass of each state and species diversity. Our analyses also provide insight into the biomass-likelihood relationship: High-biomass states have low self-inhibition and thus grow faster, outcompete others, and become much more likely. These results reveal emergent self-inhibition as a fundamental organizing principle for the attractor landscape of complex ecosystems—and provide a path to predict ecosystem outcomes without knowing microscopic interactions.

more.title: Spatiotemporal Quantum Advantages for Rare-Event Sampling
more.abstract: In a world fraught with uncertainty, it behooves us to consider the most disastrous possible outcomes, in order that we can best mitigate against them. Often these are extreme risk events–of high consequence, but low probability. Yet, the rarity of such events limits our ability to study them; there is a paucity of past occurrences to draw upon, and sampling such rare events from models is typically costly in time. Here, we introduce an approach for rare-event sampling based on quantum stochastic models. This integrates the memory advantages of quantum stochastic modeling—and its associated efficient means of preparing quantum sample states—with the “speedups” of quantum amplitude amplification, to yield simultaneous reductions in spatial and temporal computational complexity compared to classical Monte Carlo–based approaches.

more.title: An Adaptive Approach for Modeling Collisionless Plasma Shocks and Ion Heating in the Shock Frame
more.abstract: We present a novel computational method for hybrid (kinetic ions, quasi-neutral fluid electrons) simulations of nonrelativistic magnetized collisionless plasma shocks, observed near the Sun, in the solar system, and beyond. This Adaptive Frame-Of-Reference Approach enables simulations of shocks in their comoving frames of reference, where shock evolution remains quasi-steady for quasi-stationary upstream conditions, in contrast to moving shocks. We demonstrate our method in two spatial dimensions for a range of angles between the background magnetic field and the shock normal (obliquities). Shock-frame simulations, conducted with a time-adaptive hybrid code, Hybrid Parallel Event-Resolving Simulator, are shown to self-consistently capture upstream and downstream magnetic fluctuations commonly observed by spacecraft at interplanetary (IP) shocks and Earth’s bow shock. These fluctuations, which may be crucial for estimating the efficiency of ion acceleration at heliospheric and astrophysical shocks, are notably missing from many hybrid simulations of shocks, unless upstream external turbulence is imposed. The quasi-stationary behavior of numerical shocks in the shock frame is confirmed in a series of animations and by demonstrating converged ion energy spectra in the downstream region. Our approach underscores computationally efficient and physically more accurate modeling of shock-driven turbulence, downstream plasma relaxation, and concomitant ion heating in the shock frame. The new method can be used for exploring ion relaxation at IP shocks, more efficient studies of cosmic rays and plasma turbulence, and more accurate predictions of seed populations of solar energetic particles at heliospheric shocks driven by coronal mass ejections.

more.title: Dependence of Mars Solar Wind Proton Precipitation on the Interplanetary Magnetic Field Orientation: Hybrid Simulations
more.abstract: The small induced magnetosphere of Mars sometimes fails to completely screen the solar wind from precipitating on the exobase. The precipitation serves as an additional channel for mass, momentum, and energy coupling. Since the plasma flow around Mars is governed by the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) orientation and its associated convective electric field, the IMF orientation is expected to modulate the proton precipitation and the resulting coupling channel. Using a hybrid plasma model (particle ions, fluid electrons), we investigate how the precipitating protons and associated energy precipitation rates vary with upstream IMF cone angle, the angle between the solar wind velocity direction and the IMF direction. We quantify the precipitation rates by analyzing global maps of downward proton fluxes under different IMF cone angles. Our results show that proton precipitation exhibits strong sensitivity to IMF orientation. Precipitation fluxes and rates increase monotonically from perpendicular IMF through Parker spiral and cone angle 30° configurations, peaking under radial IMF conditions. While the downward rate decreases as the inner boundary is approached, the net precipitation rate remains constant. Under perpendicular and Parker spiral IMF orientations, the net precipitation rates stabilize at ∼10 22 s −1 . In contrast, the radial IMF condition drives a dramatic enhancement of 2 orders of magnitude, with the rates reaching ∼10 24 s −1 . For the cone angle 30°, Parker spiral, and perpendicular IMF conditions, proton precipitation is consistently stronger in the – E sw hemisphere. However, for the radial IMF condition, proton precipitation is enhanced in the + E sw hemisphere, which experiences more pronounced magnetospheric degeneration.

more.title: Pair-rich Corona of an Accreting Kerr Black Hole
more.abstract: We build a self-consistent model of a warm scattering corona near an accreting black hole (BH) in Kerr geometry, in the regime of slow (∼0.01 Eddington) mass accretion. This allows us to probe quantitatively the influence of relativistic gravity, BH spin, disk geometry, and photon seeding mechanism on the X-ray spectrum and polarization, for a range of observer orientation. An iterative Monte Carlo procedure is developed that incorporates self-consistently the effects of Compton scattering and electron-positron pair creation, as well as general relativistic lensing and frame dragging effects. Soft thermal photons are seeded in the inner disk and the velocity dispersion of the electrons and positrons adjusted to yield a fixed seed luminosity amplification through Compton scattering. A simple kinematic prescription is also added for bulk outflow. Pair creation by photon collisions raises significantly the density of scattering charges in and around the innermost ion disk, which is assumed to be geometrically thick and rarefied compared with the disk outside 10 gravitational radii. The self-consistent pair cloud is concentrated closer to the BH. The temperature and Compton parameter measured from the output spectra using the compPS package are consistent with fits to binary BH data in the hardest spectral state; the polarization degree rises to 4%–10% through the 2–8 keV band with allowance for e ± upflow from the BH equator.

more.title: Probing the Interstellar Medium toward the Double Pulsar and the Gum Nebula Using Low-frequency Pulse Broadening Measurements
more.abstract: Long-term timing of the double pulsar system (PSR J0737−3039A/B) has enabled some of the most stringent constraints on strong-field gravity. Yet, despite the system’s high profile, there have been very few observations at frequencies below 300 MHz, where pulse broadening due to interstellar scattering becomes significant. Measurements of the pulse broadening timescale and its frequency scaling, τ s ∝ ν α (where α is the scattering spectral index), provide valuable constraints on the structure of the scattering medium. Here we report on simultaneous observations of J0737−3039A and five other nearby pulsars (J0630−2834, J0742−2822, J0820−4114, J0835−4510, and J0837−4135) in the frequency range 109–231 MHz using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA). These observations have enabled the highest-quality detections ever published for these pulsars at low frequencies. For J0737−3039A, J0742−2822, and J0837−4135, we measure α to be −4.1(1), −3.8(1), and −4.1(1), respectively. These measurements provide new constraints on the density and turbulence parameters of the Gum Nebula region, and we discuss implications for models of the Galactic electron density distribution. Our current data yield a dispersion measure (DM) precision of ∼4 × 10 −4 cm −3 pc for J0737−3039A, which can be further improved with the MWA Phase III to reach ∼1 × 10 −4 cm −3 pc, far exceeding the precision of previous studies. The prospects for precisely constraining temporal variations in the DM and pulse broadening timescale strengthen the importance of regular monitoring of J0737−3039A at low frequencies, with the eventual goal of contributing to long-term timing studies.

more.title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.

more.title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

more.title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase. PdfB generates a transient, electrophilic oxazolone intermediate that undergoes spontaneous racemization, acting as a synthetic hub for nucleophilic attack. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these N-acyl amides exhibit potent stereospecific antiangiogenic activity by enhancing von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL)-associated proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α. This study expands the functional repertoire of ThiF-like enzymes and establishes a new conceptual framework for stereochemical diversification in bacterial metabolism, connecting microbial scalemization with the regulation of host hypoxia signaling.

more.title: Asymmetric NIR-II Voltage-Sensitive Dyes Enable Through-Skull Single-Cell Voltage Recordings of Neurons
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Optical measurements of neuronal membrane voltage in vivo are limited by light scattering at visible wavelengths. Fluorophores operating in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) offer improved tissue penetration; however, the reported NIR-II dyes generally lack voltage sensitivity because their dynamic symmetric structures disfavor field-sensitive charge separation. Here, we report a chemically optimized family of asymmetric NIR-II voltage-sensitive dyes. The optimized probe shows 20% fluorescence changes per 100 mV and submillisecond response kinetics, together with membrane-associated fluorescence enhancement that suppresses the background. In combination with oblique NIR-II light-sheet microscopy, the probes enable through-skull recording of spontaneous and sensory-evoked neuronal spiking at single-cell resolution in the mouse cortex at depths of ∼200–300 μm in real time, resolving fast neural spike trains. These results establish an asymmetric NIR-II fluorophore design as a route for minimally invasive optical voltage imaging in vivo.

more.title: Tropical land-use intensification reshapes biodiversity in expected and unexpected ways
more.abstract: Global agricultural demand has increased over the past few decades, driving land-use intensification in some of the world’s most biodiverse regions. An assessment of some 40,000 species, from soil microorganisms to vertebrates, in Sumatra, Indonesia, reveals that agricultural intensification threatens biodiversity through species loss and changes in community composition across different spatial scales. A survey of 40,000 species in Sumatra, Indonesia, could inform conservation efforts.

more.title: Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
more.abstract: As global energy markets grapple with a period of sustained political volatility, researchers are digging deep for solutions.

more.title: Bacteria and viruses team up to hasten the demise of algal blooms
more.abstract: Algal blooms are important ecological phenomena that drive carbon fixation and fuel the marine food web. Viral infection often ends them abruptly. Some bacteria can sense infected algal cells and then act in synergy with viruses to expedite a bloom’s collapse.

more.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
more.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

more.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
more.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

more.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
more.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

more.title: Poxviruses probably evolved in the digestive system of animals
more.abstract: Large and giant DNA viruses that infect unicellular eukaryotes are abundant in the environment but have rarely been found in the gut microbiome. The discovery of such viruses that prevail in the digestive system of humans and animals exposes a long-overlooked facet of the gut microbiome that clarifies the origin of poxviruses. Newly discovered viruses distributed in animal digestive systems are the closest known relatives of the clade containing smallpox virus.

more.title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
more.abstract: This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

more.title: Asymmetric Amyloid Cross-Seeding Beyond “Like-Seeds-Like”
more.abstract: Amyloid cross-seeding has often been viewed as a “like-seeds-like” extension of homologous nucleation, in which structurally similar amyloid proteins reciprocally accelerate assembly through a shared cross-β architecture. Increasing evidence instead reveals frequent asymmetry: A→B and B→A can differ in rate, mechanism, structural outcome, and biological consequence, and may change with seed state, fibril polymorph, or microenvironment. Here, we propose that productive cross-seeding is governed by directionally selective compatibility rather than generic β-sheet similarity. We examine six mechanistic origins of asymmetry: conformational selection and population shift, fibril-end templating, dock-and-lock kinetic gating, lateral-face recognition, surface-catalyzed secondary nucleation, and coaggregation coupled to strain selection. We integrate kinetic, structural, cellular, animal, and human evidence, emphasizing that bulk aggregation measurements alone cannot distinguish templated elongation from secondary nucleation, adsorption, sequestration, coaggregation, or strain conversion. We further discuss how heterotypic interfaces reshape fibril polymorphism and disease relevance, and assess emerging molecular-simulation and machine-learning approaches for predicting directional cross-seeding. This mechanism-centered framework provides a basis for understanding mixed amyloid pathologies and for developing strategies to block, redirect, or exploit heterotypic propagation in disease.

more.title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
more.abstract: Selective radical coupling of two independent unsaturated molecules poses a distinct reaction-design problem: each π-component must be assigned a different role in the reaction sequence while homocoupling, oligomerisation and polymerisation are suppressed. This review introduces the 2m/2π framework, in which two molecular components and two reactive π-bonds are assembled into a discrete product, and uses it to organise intermolecular radical reactions of alkenes and alkynes. Rather than classifying transformations primarily by reagent or catalyst, we analyse the factors that differentiate the π-components: radical polarity matching, group-transfer events, direct redox resolution, bond multiplicity, reversible radical addition and metal-supported activation. Electrophilic-, nucleophilic- and metal-hydride-initiated ene-ene cascades are compared with group-transfer radical addition, redox-driven couplings and the less developed ene-yne and yne-ene manifolds. Particular attention is paid to the origins of chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity, the termination pathways that prevent uncontrolled propagation and the substrate limitations of each strategy. The resulting framework connects previously separate reaction classes, identifies underexplored yne-yne and asymmetric coupling space, and provides practical design principles for selective multicomponent radical assembly.

more.title: Luminescent materials based on aromatic bisimides—part 1: the smaller pyromellitic and naphthalene derivatives
more.abstract: In this review, we have gathered insights into the advancements in the development and application of small aromatic bis(dicarboximide) compounds, with a particular focus on their fluorescence, thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), room temperature phosphorescence (RTP), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties. Traditionally, a low fluorescence quantum yield (QY), which is characteristic of the parent pyromellitic and naphthalene bisimides, has been viewed as a disadvantage for optoelectronic applications. However, emerging research highlighted in this review indicates that these properties can actually be beneficial due to the efficient harvesting of triplet excitons. This can be achieved in several ways, such as embedding aromatic bisimides in rigid polymeric or supramolecular matrices, utilizing the heavy-atom effect, or through tailored charge-transfer (CT) complexation with electron-rich (hetero-)aromatics. As a result, recent studies on small aromatic bisimides have established them as an important class of functional materials for generating photoluminescence across a wide spectral range and for applications in photocatalysis.

more.title: From Cold War Politics to Hot Domestic Politics — The Epidemic Intelligence Service at 75
more.abstract: The Epidemic Intelligence Service has long facilitated responses to infectious threats and other health crises. But the politicization of epidemiologic work imperils its future.

more.title: The Unexamined Subsidy — Rethinking Incentives for Outpatient Clinical Preceptors
more.abstract: States are directing substantial public funds to community physicians serving as outpatient clinical preceptors for medical schools. But recruitment incentives aren’t necessarily the best approach.

more.title: Two Ways of Seeing
more.abstract: To a new medical student, the human body may seem beautiful inside and out, yet uninterpretable. Induction into the craft of medicine is in part the process of training the eye to see differently.

more.title: What the Robot Still Can’t Do
more.abstract: A primary care physician, stumped by a patient’s chronic condition, turns to AI for a diagnosis and treatment recommendation — but discovers the essential role that must still be played by a human doctor.

more.title: Solution of a chaotic neural network at fixed connectivity
more.abstract: We calculate the moments and response functions of a nonlinear random recurrent neural network in the large- N limit using a diagrammatic technique. Our approach does not require averaging over synaptic weights and gives the first nontrivial term in a 1 / N expansion of general intensive-order correlation functions, proving a recent conjecture by Shen and Hu as a special case. Our results provide an analytical link between synaptic connectivity, correlations in spontaneous activity, and the response of a network to small perturbations.

more.title: Nonclassical Turing instabilities induced by superdiffusive transport in FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics
more.abstract: We investigate diffusion-driven instabilities in a modified FitzHugh–Nagumo-type activator–inhibitor system with superdiffusive transport modeled by fractional Laplacian operators with different diffusion orders for the activator and the inhibitor. A linear stability analysis yields explicit expressions for the instability threshold and the critical wavenumber and shows that superdiffusion modifies the band of unstable modes and the characteristic spatial scale of emerging patterns. We show that the threshold depends only on the ratio of the fractional exponents, on the kinetic parameters and on the reaction–transport parameter Γ , while it is independent of the individual diffusion orders once their ratio is fixed. The spatial scale is controlled by the diffusion orders and the domain size. When the two species have different fractional diffusion orders, their relative transport strength becomes wavelength-dependent. In particular, when the inhibitor has the higher fractional diffusion order, stationary instabilities may arise even when the scaled inhibitor-to-activator transport parameter is below unity, a regime excluded by the classical activator–inhibitor Turing criterion. A weakly nonlinear analysis near threshold provides the amplitude equation governing nonlinear saturation and reveals that superdiffusion promotes subcritical behavior. We also analyze the interaction between stationary and oscillatory instabilities near Turing–Hopf codimension-two points. All analytical results are supported by numerical simulations.

more.title: Collective Many-Body Dynamics in a Solid-State Quantum Sensor Controlled through Nanoscale Magnetic Gradients
more.abstract: Coherent collective dynamics of strongly interacting qubits are a central resource in quantum information science, with applications from quantum computing and simulation to metrology. While electronic spins interact strongly via dipolar couplings in dense solid-state ensembles, imperfections and positional disorder pose major obstacles to coherent correlated behavior, limiting their usefulness. Here, we realize collective many-body dynamics by combining time-dependent magnetic field gradients with global coherent control of dense electron spin ensembles in diamond. We control and probe the dynamics of nanometer-scale spin spirals, and, by exploiting Hamiltonian engineering that enhances the microscopic symmetry of the interactions, we observe a disorder-resilient collective spin evolution. Our results establish a pathway to interaction-enhanced quantum metrology and nanoscale imaging of materials and biological systems under ambient conditions.

more.title: Observation of Topological Berry Phases with a Single Phonon in an Ion Microtrap Array
more.abstract: Controlled quantum mechanical motion of trapped atomic ions can be used to simulate and explore collective quantum phenomena and to process quantum information. Groups of cold atomic ions confined in an externally applied trapping potential self-organize into “Coulomb crystals” due to their mutual electrostatic repulsion. The motion of the ions in these crystals is strongly coupled, and most eigenmodes of motion involve multiple ions. While this enables studies of many-body physics, it limits the flexibility and tunability of the system as a quantum platform. Here, we demonstrate an array of trapped ions in individual trapping sites whose motional modes can be controllably coupled and decoupled by locally tuning the confining potential for each ion. A single motional quantum, or phonon, can be coherently shared among two or three ions located at the vertices of an equilateral triangle 30 μ m on a side. We tune the motional eigenmodes about closed contours in configuration space and observe that, if the contour adiabatically encircles a conical intersection present in the motional eigenvalue surfaces, the single-phonon wave function acquires a topological Berry phase that is independent of the contour shape. We characterize these phases by single-phonon interference and study how phase changes occur when the motional mode tuning becomes nonadiabatic. Our results show that precise, individual quantum control of ion motion in a two-dimensional array provides unique access to quantum multibody effects.

more.title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial
more.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand. RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2…

more.title: Mediterranean low-salinity and anoxic sapropel events triggered by Atlantic atmospheric moisture
more.abstract: The Mediterranean is a saline sea because it exports moisture to the atmosphere1. Over the last million years, however, the Mediterranean has experienced abrupt declines in salinity that have collapsed the deep thermohaline circulation and caused bottom water anoxia each time the Earth has approached perihelion during the northern hemisphere summer2,3. For decades, this has been attributed to freshwater discharge from the Nile or increased precipitation in the Mediterranean basin2,3. However, the impact of past changes in the atmospheric moisture balance has been little explored. In this study, we show that these low salinity episodes were triggered by a reduced net export of moisture to the atmosphere due to enhanced mid-latitude Atlantic atmospheric water transport, affecting its salinity, deep ventilation and water exchange with the Atlantic. This conclusion is supported by the observation of low surface salinity events in the westernmost Mediterranean coinciding with events of heavy winter precipitation along the Atlantic Iberian Margin, which is the main gateway of moisture into the Mediterranean. These events were triggered by equatorward shifts of the main route of atmospheric rivers during persistent negative phases of the Arctic Oscillation at times of boreal summer insolation maxima.

more.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
more.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

more.title: A framework for modelling Population III stars in cosmological simulations
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Population III (Pop III) stars are the first generation of stars to form in the universe, emerging from primordial gas composed mainly of hydrogen and helium. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for modelling Pop III stars in cosmological simulations. This includes: (1) an enhanced thermochemical network that tracks the equilibrium abundances of H₂^+ and H^- which catalyses H₂ formation in primordial gas; (2) detailed stellar spectra of Pop III stars computed from MESA evolutionary tracks and TLUSTY NLTE atmosphere models; and (3) comprehensive supernova feedback, including both Core-Collapse and Pair-Instability supernovae, with detailed elemental yields. We implement these improvements in AREPO-RT and test them using cosmological zoom-in simulations of a 1.07 × 1010M⊙ halo at z = 3 with varying Pop III IMF. Our results show that Pop III stars form at z > 13 and are under 1 percent of new stars by z ∼ 5. Their Lyman-Werner radiation raises the local LW flux by two orders of magnitude at z ≈ 16, and their feedback lowers the star formation rate at z > 5.5. The new chemistry more than doubles the mass fraction of cool, dense pristine gas, while Pop III feedback creates photo-heated diffuse gas and drives distinct metal enrichment patterns at 10 < z < 6. The choice of IMF for Pop III stars critically determines the balance between radiative and mechanical feedback, with top-heavy choices producing stronger feedback and more metals but retaining less metal-enriched gas within the halo. Only runs with top-heavy IMFs produce high He ii equivalent-width (> 20 Å) comparable with JWST observations from a galaxy at z ∼ 11.

more.title: Pulse profile modelling of accreting millisecond pulsars with disc occultation and its impact on parameter inference
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Pulse profile modelling is a relativistic ray-tracing technique used to infer neutron star mass, radius, and surface hotspot properties from X-ray pulsations. Pulse profile modelling has been widely applied to rotation-powered millisecond pulsars, where the local environment is relatively empty. Application to accreting millisecond pulsars is complicated by the geometry of the local accretion flow, including disc occultation of surface emission. In this work, we extend an established pulse profile modelling code, X-PSI, to incorporate accretion disc occultation in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling. We quantify how disc occultation depends on system geometry and evaluate its impact on parameter inference. We find that disc occultation is primarily governed by the viewing inclination and can significantly reshape pulse profiles at moderate to high inclinations. Using synthetic Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer datasets, we investigate parameter recovery for two representative hotspot configurations. For hotspots close to the rotational poles, statistically acceptable fits can yield posteriors that deviate noticeably from the true parameters. In contrast, in a case with hotspots located closer to the equator we find more reliable parameter recovery. We further find that neglecting disc occultation can introduce spurious posterior modes with comparable statistical support, potentially affecting the interpretation of inferred neutron star parameters, suggesting that this effect should be included in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling.

more.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
more.abstract: Dementia incidence has been declining in Western societies for decades, but whether this reflects higher cognitive capacity entering old age, slower cognitive decline, or both remains unresolved. Analysing ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals across five longitudinal cohorts, we find that later-born cohorts benefit from a double dividend: higher memory levels entering old age and slower rates of decline. The projected 20-year cohort advantage at age 80 is of sufficient magnitude to plausibly account for the observed 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence reported in meta-analyses. Generational gains are disproportionately concentrated among the fastest-declining individuals, and are reflected in lower hippocampal atrophy rates in an independent sample. A formal bounding analysis shows that the double dividend is robust across a range of plausible period assumptions, consistent with environmental conditions operating across the lifespan having reshaped the architecture of human cognitive aging.

more.title: The assembly and fate of a giant disc galaxy in a protocluster at z = 3
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Recent JWST observations revealed two massive (M⋆ ≳ 1011 M⊙), unexpectedly large spiral galaxies at z ∼ 3, both in overdense environments. We focus on one of these, ADF22.A1 at z = 3.09, which hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN), exploiting its extended [CII] emission (∼30 kpc in diameter) with high-resolution observations from the Atacama Large Millimetre Array and JWST. We find a flat outer rotation curve reaching ∼530 km s−1, and perform, for the first time for a system of this type, a rotation-curve decomposition. We infer a dark-matter halo mass of log (M₂₀₀/M_⊙)=12.9^(+0.4)_(-0.3), a baryon-to-halo mass ratio of 0.4^(+0.6)_(-0.3) in units of the cosmological baryon fraction, and a ratio between the baryonic and dark-matter halo specific angular momentum of 1.0^(+0.7)_(-0.5). Comparing these quantities with those of local galaxies, we find that ADF22.A1 is indistinguishable from z = 0 giant discs, pointing to the inefficiency of AGN feedback in halting disc growth. Using the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey, we identify potential z = 0 descendants of ADF22.A1, suggesting it will evolve into an extreme (in either mass or angular momentum) early-type galaxy. Finally, we argue that cold-stream accretion, invoked to explain disc formation at z > 1, is disfavoured as the primary formation channel: while not formally excluded, it struggles to account simultaneously for the observed morphology, size, dynamical properties, high specific angular momentum, and baryon-to-halo mass ratio. Instead, sustained accretion from the hot circumgalactic medium offers a plausible, and possibly favoured, alternative.

more.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
more.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

shortlist.title: Learning functions of Hamiltonians with Hamiltonian Fourier features
shortlist.abstract: We propose a quantum machine learning task that is provably easy for quantum computers and hard for classical ones. The task involves predicting quantities of the form T r [ f ( H ) ρ ] , where f is an unknown function, given descriptions of H and ρ . Using a Fourier-based feature map of Hamiltonians and linear regression, we theoretically establish the learnability of the task and implement it on a superconducting device using up to 72 qubits. This work provides a machine learning task with practical relevance, provable quantum easiness, and near-term feasibility.

shortlist.title: Floquet Engineering of a Quasiequilibrium Superradiant Phase Transition in Landau Polaritons
shortlist.abstract: Superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs), characterized by photon condensation and macroscopic matter polarization, are forbidden in equilibrium for homogeneous fields by no-go theorems. Here, we show that Floquet driving can circumvent this constraint in a Landau polariton system consisting of a two-dimensional electron gas coupled to a terahertz cavity in a DC magnetic field. An off-resonant AC magnetic field modulates the cyclotron frequency and light-matter coupling strength while leaving the diamagnetic term unchanged, generating an additional DC coupling contribution. This drives the system across a critical threshold into a superradiant phase, characterized by photon condensation and Landau-level polarization in the ground state of the Floquet Hamiltonian. This quasiequilibrium approach offers a route to SRPTs distinct from driven-dissipative schemes.

shortlist.title: Plasma Conductivity from Warm Dense Matter to the Spitzer Limit Using Mean-Force Kinetic Theory
shortlist.abstract: A theoretical model is developed to compute electronic transport coefficients extending from warm and dense to hot and dilute plasma conditions. This kinetic theory-based approach models strong Coulomb correlations by treating collisions using the potential of mean force, electron degeneracy using the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation, and diffraction by computing cross sections quantum mechanically. Hydrodynamic transport coefficients are computed by solving the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation using the Chapman-Enskog method. The result provides a fast and accurate means to compute electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and electrothermal coefficients, including contributions from electron-electron collisions. The model enables accurate calculation of materials properties in many warm dense matter systems, including inertial confinement fusion, stellar evolution, and high energy density plasma experiments.

shortlist.title: Study of K S 0 a 0 ( 980 ) 0 and K ‾ * ( 892 ) 0 η in the D 0 → K S 0 π 0 η decay
shortlist.abstract: We perform an amplitude analysis of the decay D 0 → K S 0 π 0 η and measure its absolute branching fraction to be ( 1.016 ± 0.013 stat. ± 0.014 syst. ) % . The analysis utilizes 20.3 fb − 1 of e + e − collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV with the BESIII detector. We precisely determine ℬ ( D 0 → K S 0 a 0 ( 980 ) 0 , a 0 ( 980 ) 0 → π 0 η ) = ( 9.47 ± 0.36 stat. ± 0.40 syst. ) × 10 − 3 , improving the precision of the world average by a factor of 4.5. Combined with our previous result, these measurements differ from q q ‾ model predictions by an order of magnitude but agree well with tetraquark predictions, strongly supporting the a 0 ( 980 ) as a tetraquark state. Furthermore, the branching fraction of the intermediate process D 0 → K ‾ * ( 892 ) 0 η is determined to be ( 0.70 ± 0.05 stat. ± 0.03 syst. ) % , which is 5 σ smaller than the result measured in D 0 → K − π + η by the Belle experiment. As a result, the magnitudes of the W -exchange and QCD-penguin amplitudes are found to be less than half of their current estimations.

shortlist.title: A JWST/NIRSpec Catalog of Low-mass Candidates toward NGC 2024 from Multicomponent Spectral Modeling
shortlist.abstract: Young low-mass objects in crowded, highly obscured star-forming regions are difficult to characterize. Deriving reliable physical parameters requires separating photospheric emission from complex extinction and circumstellar emission. We apply a multicomponent spectral-modeling framework to JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra toward NGC 2024, obtaining adopted fits for 78 sources. The framework incorporates atmospheric models, dust and ice opacities, and optional thermal emission. Most spectra favor additional large-H 2 O-ice opacity over the baseline small-grain model, while a smaller subset requires additional gray opacity, potentially arising from large refractory grains. Some spectra also require a thermal component to reproduce the long-wavelength continuum. The parameters inferred with this framework, together with the NGC 2024 distance, yield radii and bolometric luminosities. Comparison with evolutionary models for young low-mass and substellar objects provides mass estimates and identifies 46 candidate members, 27 sources classified as background, and 5 uncertain sources. Candidate members show lower fitted surface gravities than likely background stars. Of the candidate members, 23 lie above the youngest available isochrones, plausibly reflecting the cluster’s youth and uncertainties in model initial conditions. The resulting catalog provides a uniform characterization of the NGC 2024 sample and establishes a framework for treating complex extinction and circumstellar emission in JWST spectra of other obscured star-forming regions.

shortlist.title: The Luminosity Function and Isotropic Energy Function of Long Gamma-Ray Bursts in the Comoving Frame
shortlist.abstract: We study the comoving-frame properties of 77 long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with initial Lorentz factor (Γ 0 ) estimates, including parameter distributions, spectral-energy correlations, luminosity functions, and isotropic energy functions. Specifically, the comoving-frame distributions are significantly narrower than those in the rest frame, while the Amati and Yonetoku relations still exist but become considerably weaker, indicating that relativistic Doppler effects contribute strongly to the observed correlations. Using the Lynden-Bell c − method, we find significant redshift evolution of both luminosity and isotropic energy, with consistent evolution indices within statistical uncertainties in each frame, implying that LGRB duration may not exhibit significant redshift evolution. After de-evolution, the luminosity functions are well described by triple power laws in both frames. In contrast, the isotropic energy function changes from a broken power law in the rest frame to a triple power law in the comoving frame, with much steeper high-energy tails. This indicates that the energy-function shape in previous works is strongly affected by Γ 0 and suggests an effective upper envelope in the comoving-frame energy scale. Overall, our results demonstrate that the Γ 0 correction is essential for revealing the intrinsic properties of LGRBs.

shortlist.title: An Adaptive Approach for Modeling Collisionless Plasma Shocks and Ion Heating in the Shock Frame
shortlist.abstract: We present a novel computational method for hybrid (kinetic ions, quasi-neutral fluid electrons) simulations of nonrelativistic magnetized collisionless plasma shocks, observed near the Sun, in the solar system, and beyond. This Adaptive Frame-Of-Reference Approach enables simulations of shocks in their comoving frames of reference, where shock evolution remains quasi-steady for quasi-stationary upstream conditions, in contrast to moving shocks. We demonstrate our method in two spatial dimensions for a range of angles between the background magnetic field and the shock normal (obliquities). Shock-frame simulations, conducted with a time-adaptive hybrid code, Hybrid Parallel Event-Resolving Simulator, are shown to self-consistently capture upstream and downstream magnetic fluctuations commonly observed by spacecraft at interplanetary (IP) shocks and Earth’s bow shock. These fluctuations, which may be crucial for estimating the efficiency of ion acceleration at heliospheric and astrophysical shocks, are notably missing from many hybrid simulations of shocks, unless upstream external turbulence is imposed. The quasi-stationary behavior of numerical shocks in the shock frame is confirmed in a series of animations and by demonstrating converged ion energy spectra in the downstream region. Our approach underscores computationally efficient and physically more accurate modeling of shock-driven turbulence, downstream plasma relaxation, and concomitant ion heating in the shock frame. The new method can be used for exploring ion relaxation at IP shocks, more efficient studies of cosmic rays and plasma turbulence, and more accurate predictions of seed populations of solar energetic particles at heliospheric shocks driven by coronal mass ejections.

shortlist.title: Dependence of Mars Solar Wind Proton Precipitation on the Interplanetary Magnetic Field Orientation: Hybrid Simulations
shortlist.abstract: The small induced magnetosphere of Mars sometimes fails to completely screen the solar wind from precipitating on the exobase. The precipitation serves as an additional channel for mass, momentum, and energy coupling. Since the plasma flow around Mars is governed by the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) orientation and its associated convective electric field, the IMF orientation is expected to modulate the proton precipitation and the resulting coupling channel. Using a hybrid plasma model (particle ions, fluid electrons), we investigate how the precipitating protons and associated energy precipitation rates vary with upstream IMF cone angle, the angle between the solar wind velocity direction and the IMF direction. We quantify the precipitation rates by analyzing global maps of downward proton fluxes under different IMF cone angles. Our results show that proton precipitation exhibits strong sensitivity to IMF orientation. Precipitation fluxes and rates increase monotonically from perpendicular IMF through Parker spiral and cone angle 30° configurations, peaking under radial IMF conditions. While the downward rate decreases as the inner boundary is approached, the net precipitation rate remains constant. Under perpendicular and Parker spiral IMF orientations, the net precipitation rates stabilize at ∼10 22 s −1 . In contrast, the radial IMF condition drives a dramatic enhancement of 2 orders of magnitude, with the rates reaching ∼10 24 s −1 . For the cone angle 30°, Parker spiral, and perpendicular IMF conditions, proton precipitation is consistently stronger in the – E sw hemisphere. However, for the radial IMF condition, proton precipitation is enhanced in the + E sw hemisphere, which experiences more pronounced magnetospheric degeneration.

shortlist.title: Investigation of Cu(II) Binding by Human Calprotectin Reveals an Unusual Fluxional Coordination Environment
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Human calprotectin (CP, S100A8/S100A9 heterooligomer) is a multi-metal sequestering protein that contributes to the innate immune response by starving invading microbial pathogens of essential metal nutrients. Despite the ability of CP to withhold copper from microbial pathogens, its copper coordination chemistry is largely unexplored. Here we elucidate the Cu(II)-binding properties of CP-Ser [S100A8(C42S)/S100A9(C3S) variant] under conditions of high and low Ca(II) and present a working model for how CP sequesters Cu(II). Our biochemical and spectroscopic studies reveal that both the His3Asp and His6 sites bind Cu(II) with Ca(II)-dependent affinity, and Cu(II) binding to both sites is required for Cu(II)-dependent self-association of CP heterodimers to heterotetramers. Moreover, our spectroscopic data demonstrate that Cu(II) binds to the His6 site in a fluxional coordination environment, and that the mode of Cu(II) binding is allosterically modulated by Ca(II) coordination to the EF-hand domains and Cu(II) binding at the His3Asp site. Sequestration of Cu(II) using a fluxional His6 site contrasts with how CP captures other nutrient M(II) (M = Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn) at this site using a static and nearly idealized octahedral binding mode. This study reveals the remarkable ability of a fluxional site to participate in metal sequestration at the host-pathogen interface.

shortlist.title: Good Practices and Common Pitfalls in the Research and Development of New Electrolytes for Flow Batteries
shortlist.abstract: Redox flow batteries represent one of the most actively investigated platforms for grid-scale electrochemical energy storage. The rapid expansion of electrolyte chemistries has broadened the field, but has also introduced significant inconsistencies in experimental methods, testing protocols, and reporting practices. This variability impedes interlaboratory comparison and, in some cases, produces misleading assessments of electrolyte performance and stability. This article presents structured, practical guidance for researchers working with novel flow battery electrolytes, organized around four core activities: electrolyte formulation and physicochemical characterization, electroanalytical screening, flow cell assembly and hardware selection, and performance and lifetime evaluation. Key topics include staged characterization of redox-active compounds from dilute cyclic voltammetry through operationally relevant conditions, component selection and compatibility checks, the distinction between symmetric and full cell configurations for performance versus lifetime testing, and the role of potentiostatic cycling protocols in generating reliable capacity fade data. Finally, the reporting of capacity fade is discussed with consideration of the underlying degradation mechanisms. The guidance is condensed into ten practical recommendations, and the article is published as a living document on GitHub, open to continuous community revision and peer review to work toward a community consensus on experimental and reporting practices in our field.

shortlist.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
shortlist.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1–3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4–7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse. Single-cell epigenetic analyses reveal a conserved epigenetic signature across patients that may help identify those at increased risk for disease relapse in breast cancer.

shortlist.title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.

shortlist.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
shortlist.abstract: Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.
