shortlist.title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

shortlist.title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase. PdfB generates a transient, electrophilic oxazolone intermediate that undergoes spontaneous racemization, acting as a synthetic hub for nucleophilic attack. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these N-acyl amides exhibit potent stereospecific antiangiogenic activity by enhancing von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL)-associated proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α. This study expands the functional repertoire of ThiF-like enzymes and establishes a new conceptual framework for stereochemical diversification in bacterial metabolism, connecting microbial scalemization with the regulation of host hypoxia signaling.

shortlist.title: Tropical land-use intensification reshapes biodiversity in expected and unexpected ways
shortlist.abstract: Global agricultural demand has increased over the past few decades, driving land-use intensification in some of the world’s most biodiverse regions. An assessment of some 40,000 species, from soil microorganisms to vertebrates, in Sumatra, Indonesia, reveals that agricultural intensification threatens biodiversity through species loss and changes in community composition across different spatial scales. A survey of 40,000 species in Sumatra, Indonesia, could inform conservation efforts.

shortlist.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
shortlist.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

shortlist.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
shortlist.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

shortlist.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
shortlist.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

shortlist.title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
shortlist.abstract: This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

shortlist.title: Asymmetric Amyloid Cross-Seeding Beyond “Like-Seeds-Like”
shortlist.abstract: Amyloid cross-seeding has often been viewed as a “like-seeds-like” extension of homologous nucleation, in which structurally similar amyloid proteins reciprocally accelerate assembly through a shared cross-β architecture. Increasing evidence instead reveals frequent asymmetry: A→B and B→A can differ in rate, mechanism, structural outcome, and biological consequence, and may change with seed state, fibril polymorph, or microenvironment. Here, we propose that productive cross-seeding is governed by directionally selective compatibility rather than generic β-sheet similarity. We examine six mechanistic origins of asymmetry: conformational selection and population shift, fibril-end templating, dock-and-lock kinetic gating, lateral-face recognition, surface-catalyzed secondary nucleation, and coaggregation coupled to strain selection. We integrate kinetic, structural, cellular, animal, and human evidence, emphasizing that bulk aggregation measurements alone cannot distinguish templated elongation from secondary nucleation, adsorption, sequestration, coaggregation, or strain conversion. We further discuss how heterotypic interfaces reshape fibril polymorphism and disease relevance, and assess emerging molecular-simulation and machine-learning approaches for predicting directional cross-seeding. This mechanism-centered framework provides a basis for understanding mixed amyloid pathologies and for developing strategies to block, redirect, or exploit heterotypic propagation in disease.

shortlist.title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
shortlist.abstract: Selective radical coupling of two independent unsaturated molecules poses a distinct reaction-design problem: each π-component must be assigned a different role in the reaction sequence while homocoupling, oligomerisation and polymerisation are suppressed. This review introduces the 2m/2π framework, in which two molecular components and two reactive π-bonds are assembled into a discrete product, and uses it to organise intermolecular radical reactions of alkenes and alkynes. Rather than classifying transformations primarily by reagent or catalyst, we analyse the factors that differentiate the π-components: radical polarity matching, group-transfer events, direct redox resolution, bond multiplicity, reversible radical addition and metal-supported activation. Electrophilic-, nucleophilic- and metal-hydride-initiated ene-ene cascades are compared with group-transfer radical addition, redox-driven couplings and the less developed ene-yne and yne-ene manifolds. Particular attention is paid to the origins of chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity, the termination pathways that prevent uncontrolled propagation and the substrate limitations of each strategy. The resulting framework connects previously separate reaction classes, identifies underexplored yne-yne and asymmetric coupling space, and provides practical design principles for selective multicomponent radical assembly.

shortlist.abstract: We calculate the moments and response functions of a nonlinear random recurrent neural network in the large- N limit using a diagrammatic technique. Our approach does not require averaging over synaptic weights and gives the first nontrivial term in a 1 / N expansion of general intensive-order correlation functions, proving a recent conjecture by Shen and Hu as a special case. Our results provide an analytical link between synaptic connectivity, correlations in spontaneous activity, and the response of a network to small perturbations.

shortlist.title: Nonclassical Turing instabilities induced by superdiffusive transport in FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics
shortlist.abstract: We investigate diffusion-driven instabilities in a modified FitzHugh–Nagumo-type activator–inhibitor system with superdiffusive transport modeled by fractional Laplacian operators with different diffusion orders for the activator and the inhibitor. A linear stability analysis yields explicit expressions for the instability threshold and the critical wavenumber and shows that superdiffusion modifies the band of unstable modes and the characteristic spatial scale of emerging patterns. We show that the threshold depends only on the ratio of the fractional exponents, on the kinetic parameters and on the reaction–transport parameter Γ , while it is independent of the individual diffusion orders once their ratio is fixed. The spatial scale is controlled by the diffusion orders and the domain size. When the two species have different fractional diffusion orders, their relative transport strength becomes wavelength-dependent. In particular, when the inhibitor has the higher fractional diffusion order, stationary instabilities may arise even when the scaled inhibitor-to-activator transport parameter is below unity, a regime excluded by the classical activator–inhibitor Turing criterion. A weakly nonlinear analysis near threshold provides the amplitude equation governing nonlinear saturation and reveals that superdiffusion promotes subcritical behavior. We also analyze the interaction between stationary and oscillatory instabilities near Turing–Hopf codimension-two points. All analytical results are supported by numerical simulations.

shortlist.title: Collective Many-Body Dynamics in a Solid-State Quantum Sensor Controlled through Nanoscale Magnetic Gradients
shortlist.abstract: Coherent collective dynamics of strongly interacting qubits are a central resource in quantum information science, with applications from quantum computing and simulation to metrology. While electronic spins interact strongly via dipolar couplings in dense solid-state ensembles, imperfections and positional disorder pose major obstacles to coherent correlated behavior, limiting their usefulness. Here, we realize collective many-body dynamics by combining time-dependent magnetic field gradients with global coherent control of dense electron spin ensembles in diamond. We control and probe the dynamics of nanometer-scale spin spirals, and, by exploiting Hamiltonian engineering that enhances the microscopic symmetry of the interactions, we observe a disorder-resilient collective spin evolution. Our results establish a pathway to interaction-enhanced quantum metrology and nanoscale imaging of materials and biological systems under ambient conditions.

shortlist.title: Observation of Topological Berry Phases with a Single Phonon in an Ion Microtrap Array
shortlist.abstract: Controlled quantum mechanical motion of trapped atomic ions can be used to simulate and explore collective quantum phenomena and to process quantum information. Groups of cold atomic ions confined in an externally applied trapping potential self-organize into “Coulomb crystals” due to their mutual electrostatic repulsion. The motion of the ions in these crystals is strongly coupled, and most eigenmodes of motion involve multiple ions. While this enables studies of many-body physics, it limits the flexibility and tunability of the system as a quantum platform. Here, we demonstrate an array of trapped ions in individual trapping sites whose motional modes can be controllably coupled and decoupled by locally tuning the confining potential for each ion. A single motional quantum, or phonon, can be coherently shared among two or three ions located at the vertices of an equilateral triangle 30 μ m on a side. We tune the motional eigenmodes about closed contours in configuration space and observe that, if the contour adiabatically encircles a conical intersection present in the motional eigenvalue surfaces, the single-phonon wave function acquires a topological Berry phase that is independent of the contour shape. We characterize these phases by single-phonon interference and study how phase changes occur when the motional mode tuning becomes nonadiabatic. Our results show that precise, individual quantum control of ion motion in a two-dimensional array provides unique access to quantum multibody effects.

shortlist.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand. RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. shortlist.title: Mediterranean low-salinity and anoxic sapropel events triggered by Atlantic atmospheric moisture
shortlist.abstract: The Mediterranean is a saline sea because it exports moisture to the atmosphere1. Over the last million years, however, the Mediterranean has experienced abrupt declines in salinity that have collapsed the deep thermohaline circulation and caused bottom water anoxia each time the Earth has approached perihelion during the northern hemisphere summer2,3. For decades, this has been attributed to freshwater discharge from the Nile or increased precipitation in the Mediterranean basin2,3. However, the impact of past changes in the atmospheric moisture balance has been little explored. In this study, we show that these low salinity episodes were triggered by a reduced net export of moisture to the atmosphere due to enhanced mid-latitude Atlantic atmospheric water transport, affecting its salinity, deep ventilation and water exchange with the Atlantic. This conclusion is supported by the observation of low surface salinity events in the westernmost Mediterranean coinciding with events of heavy winter precipitation along the Atlantic Iberian Margin, which is the main gateway of moisture into the Mediterranean. These events were triggered by equatorward shifts of the main route of atmospheric rivers during persistent negative phases of the Arctic Oscillation at times of boreal summer insolation maxima.

shortlist.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
shortlist.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

shortlist.title: A framework for modelling Population III stars in cosmological simulations
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Population III (Pop III) stars are the first generation of stars to form in the universe, emerging from primordial gas composed mainly of hydrogen and helium. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for modelling Pop III stars in cosmological simulations. This includes: (1) an enhanced thermochemical network that tracks the equilibrium abundances of H₂^+ and H^- which catalyses H₂ formation in primordial gas; (2) detailed stellar spectra of Pop III stars computed from MESA evolutionary tracks and TLUSTY NLTE atmosphere models; and (3) comprehensive supernova feedback, including both Core-Collapse and Pair-Instability supernovae, with detailed elemental yields. We implement these improvements in AREPO-RT and test them using cosmological zoom-in simulations of a 1.07 × 1010M⊙ halo at z = 3 with varying Pop III IMF. Our results show that Pop III stars form at z > 13 and are under 1 percent of new stars by z ∼ 5. Their Lyman-Werner radiation raises the local LW flux by two orders of magnitude at z ≈ 16, and their feedback lowers the star formation rate at z > 5.5. The new chemistry more than doubles the mass fraction of cool, dense pristine gas, while Pop III feedback creates photo-heated diffuse gas and drives distinct metal enrichment patterns at 10 < z < 6. The choice of IMF for Pop III stars critically determines the balance between radiative and mechanical feedback, with top-heavy choices producing stronger feedback and more metals but retaining less metal-enriched gas within the halo. Only runs with top-heavy IMFs produce high He ii equivalent-width (> 20 Å) comparable with JWST observations from a galaxy at z ∼ 11.

shortlist.title: Pulse profile modelling of accreting millisecond pulsars with disc occultation and its impact on parameter inference
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Pulse profile modelling is a relativistic ray-tracing technique used to infer neutron star mass, radius, and surface hotspot properties from X-ray pulsations. Pulse profile modelling has been widely applied to rotation-powered millisecond pulsars, where the local environment is relatively empty. Application to accreting millisecond pulsars is complicated by the geometry of the local accretion flow, including disc occultation of surface emission. In this work, we extend an established pulse profile modelling code, X-PSI, to incorporate accretion disc occultation in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling. We quantify how disc occultation depends on system geometry and evaluate its impact on parameter inference. We find that disc occultation is primarily governed by the viewing inclination and can significantly reshape pulse profiles at moderate to high inclinations. Using synthetic Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer datasets, we investigate parameter recovery for two representative hotspot configurations. For hotspots close to the rotational poles, statistically acceptable fits can yield posteriors that deviate noticeably from the true parameters. In contrast, in a case with hotspots located closer to the equator we find more reliable parameter recovery. We further find that neglecting disc occultation can introduce spurious posterior modes with comparable statistical support, potentially affecting the interpretation of inferred neutron star parameters, suggesting that this effect should be included in accreting millisecond pulsar pulse profile modelling.

shortlist.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
shortlist.abstract: Dementia incidence has been declining in Western societies for decades, but whether this reflects higher cognitive capacity entering old age, slower cognitive decline, or both remains unresolved. Analysing ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals across five longitudinal cohorts, we find that later-born cohorts benefit from a double dividend: higher memory levels entering old age and slower rates of decline. The projected 20-year cohort advantage at age 80 is of sufficient magnitude to plausibly account for the observed 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence reported in meta-analyses. Generational gains are disproportionately concentrated among the fastest-declining individuals, and are reflected in lower hippocampal atrophy rates in an independent sample. A formal bounding analysis shows that the double dividend is robust across a range of plausible period assumptions, consistent with environmental conditions operating across the lifespan having reshaped the architecture of human cognitive aging.

shortlist.title: The assembly and fate of a giant disc galaxy in a protocluster at z = 3
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Recent JWST observations revealed two massive (M⋆ ≳ 1011 M⊙), unexpectedly large spiral galaxies at z ∼ 3, both in overdense environments. We focus on one of these, ADF22.A1 at z = 3.09, which hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN), exploiting its extended [CII] emission (∼30 kpc in diameter) with high-resolution observations from the Atacama Large Millimetre Array and JWST. We find a flat outer rotation curve reaching ∼530 km s−1, and perform, for the first time for a system of this type, a rotation-curve decomposition. We infer a dark-matter halo mass of log (M₂₀₀/M_⊙)=12.9^(+0.4)_(-0.3), a baryon-to-halo mass ratio of 0.4^(+0.6)_(-0.3) in units of the cosmological baryon fraction, and a ratio between the baryonic and dark-matter halo specific angular momentum of 1.0^(+0.7)_(-0.5). Comparing these quantities with those of local galaxies, we find that ADF22.A1 is indistinguishable from z = 0 giant discs, pointing to the inefficiency of AGN feedback in halting disc growth. Using the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey, we identify potential z = 0 descendants of ADF22.A1, suggesting it will evolve into an extreme (in either mass or angular momentum) early-type galaxy. Finally, we argue that cold-stream accretion, invoked to explain disc formation at z > 1, is disfavoured as the primary formation channel: while not formally excluded, it struggles to account simultaneously for the observed morphology, size, dynamical properties, high specific angular momentum, and baryon-to-halo mass ratio. Instead, sustained accretion from the hot circumgalactic medium offers a plausible, and possibly favoured, alternative.

shortlist.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
shortlist.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

From Design to Disclosure
shortlist.abstract: We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

shortlist.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
shortlist.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. Collectively, the paper highlights the private costs and social benefits of responsible investing. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: S. Agarwal and J. shortlist.title: Corporate Contributions to Ballot Measure Campaigns: Real Effects and Valuation
shortlist.abstract: We analyze novel data on corporate contributions to ballot initiatives at the U.S. state level. Firms make large contributions to ballot measure campaigns in favor of or against specific initiatives. They contribute significantly more to business initiatives compared with ideological initiatives. Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. Contributing firms experience changes in sales growth following the passage of important ballot measures. Following successful (failed) initiatives, all firms in affected industries exhibit significantly more positive (negative) cumulative abnormal returns around the election, but contributing firms do more so than peers. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Fahlenbrach gratefully acknowledges financial support from the Swiss Finance Institute. shortlist.title: Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c–mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A′-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F′-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

shortlist.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
shortlist.abstract: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice
shortlist.abstract: Study Objectives Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group). Results IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve. Conclusions IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. shortlist.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

Effective gaps between singular values of non-stationary matrix products subject to non-degenerate noise
shortlist.abstract: We study the singular values and Lyapunov exponents of non-stationary random matrix products subject to small, absolutely continuous, additive noise. Consider a fixed sequence of matrices of bounded norm. Independently perturb the matrices by additive noise distributed according to Lebesgue measure on matrices with norm less than ε ϵ . Then the gaps between the logarithms of the singular values of the random product of n n of these matrices are all of order at least ε ²n ϵ 2 n , both in expectation; and almost surely for large n n . To prove this, we develop recent work of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn [26]. That paper gives a very flexible method, based on relative entropy, for showing that a non-stationary product of matrices in SL(d,R) SL ( d , R ) has a strictly positive Lyapunov exponent. We extend their work in two ways, firstly by making the estimates quantitative in the context of absolutely continuous distributions, giving the universal estimates described above; and secondly by developing a fibered version of their methods, working on flag bundles instead of the projective space to estimate gaps between arbitrary consecutive exponents. Our methods retain much of the flexibility of those of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn, and we hope that they will find application in other related problems.

shortlist.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance
shortlist.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver–resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

shortlist.title: Competition in Markups: A Theory of the Lerner Index in Networks and General Equilibrium
shortlist.abstract: What determines demand elasticities and markups in production networks, where firms' demand and pricing are interdependent? I propose competition in markups, an equilibrium concept in which firms choose markups, taking other firms' markups as given. In partial equilibrium with vertical structures, it links upstream demand elasticities to downstream characteristics without backward induction and ties pass-through to the curvature of final demand. In general equilibrium with arbitrary industry networks, it microfounds firms' demand elasticities and markups through their within-industry market shares and four industry-level network statistics---cycle, substitution in production, substitution in consumption, and consumer-price impact. Empirical analysis of Compustat firms from 1997 to 2019 confirms the predicted variation of industry demand elasticities and firm markups. Relative to an exogenous-markup benchmark, endogenous markups dampen the aggregate TFP impact of a productivity shock to an industry's largest firm by 6% for the median industry, and by up to 48% across industries.

Banking on a Corporate Rebrand
shortlist.abstract: Firms often rebrand to counter negative shocks, but can it work? Using a historical natural experiment, we analyze a large sample of companies from the same industry (banking) that shared very similar names, but overwhelmingly decided to change them in response to a common, negative news shock. U.S. entry into World War I in 1917 created a sudden anti-German backlash against anything that invoked an association with the now enemy. The shock itself was thus orthogonal to bank fundamentals and pre-existing trends, but pushed banks to reconsider their brands. After 1917, the few German-named banks that kept their tainted names saw significant declines in assets, deposits, and market share relative to other banks. However, German-named banks that rebranded mitigated much of the negative shock. Specifically, German-named banks that adopted a new non-ethnic brand name avoided between 75% and 85% of the anti-German effect, and those that adopted a new patriotic brand name were able to neutralize it completely. Overall, we find that “crisis rebranding” paid off in our historical setting regardless of the chosen brand, with patriotic rebranding proving the most effective at offsetting the exogenous shock. shortlist.title: The Welfare Effects of Price Shocks and Household Relief Packages: Evidence from an Energy Crisis
shortlist.abstract: Aggregate price shocks generate unequal welfare losses both across and within income groups.Policymakers face a trade-off: price subsidies direct more support to households facing larger losses, but create inefficiencies, while transfers are less distortionary but harder to target.We develop and implement a framework to quantify this trade-off using rich panel data on households' energy spending and incomes, alongside price and policy variation from the 2022-23 European Energy Crisis.Absent policy intervention, average household welfare losses would have equalled 6% of income, with some households facing much larger losses.The combination of an energy-price subsidy and universal transfers reduced both the mean and dispersion of losses, but incurred efficiency costs equal to 12% of total relief-package revenue costs.Optimal policy entails a strictly positive price subsidy, though its level is lower when transfers can be targeted using income and prior energy usage.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
fundamentals.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

fundamentals.title: Revealing temperature effects on sliding friction through many-body phonon dynamics
fundamentals.abstract: Despite centuries of research into friction through classical mechanics, the fundamental principles governing friction remain poorly understood, particularly its temperature-dependent nature. This study proposes a quantum theory that reexamines the fundamental principles of tribology. By employing the Feynman diagrammatic perturbation technique within the framework of quantum many-body theory, this study incorporates phonon-phonon interactions to capture the microscopic mechanisms of energy dissipation. The results demonstrate that the phonon radiation governed by harmonic interactions dominates energy dissipation at cryogenic temperatures. As temperature rises, phonon scattering governed by anharmonic interactions overtakes radiation as the primary dissipation mechanism. Further increases in temperature lead to greater damping and suppressed phonon excitation, thereby reducing energy dissipation. The competition among phonon radiation, phonon scattering, and phonon excitation gives rise to the non-monotonic temperature characteristics of friction. Notably, this non-monotonic temperature dependence is also reproduced by classical molecular dynamics simulations. This framework provides a unified understanding of disparate friction trends with temperature observed across different materials, offering insights into the fundamental mechanisms of frictional energy dissipation.

fundamentals.title: Dual Relaxation Modes Control Polymer Crystallization
fundamentals.abstract: Crystallization in polymers provides a fundamental probe of how molecular relaxation governs the emergence of order in glass-forming systems. Despite the longstanding success of the Lauritzen-Hoffman theory, its empirical treatment of molecular diffusion fails to capture the crystallization kinetics observed in the deeply supercooled regime. Here, we establish a physically grounded framework that replaces the empirical mobility in the Lauritzen-Hoffman formalism with a weighted combination of two measurable relaxation modes, namely the structural α relaxation, governing cooperative dynamics, and the slow Arrhenius process, associated with localized molecular rearrangements. This unified two-channel description quantitatively reproduces crystallization kinetics over several decades in time across 12 polymers spanning a wide range of fragility. In addition, our framework remains predictive under nanoconfinement, where interfaces and finite-size effects modify both mobility and nucleation. The results reveal that polymer crystallization proceeds through coupled long-range transport and localized ordering events governed by the same relaxation hierarchy that underlies vitrification, thus bridging glassy dynamics and crystallization kinetics at the molecular level.

fundamentals.title: Ordering of oxygen atoms in titanium revealed by superresolution electron ptychography
fundamentals.abstract: Interstitial atoms such as oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen are common point defects in crystalline solids and play important roles in determining electronic and mechanical properties. For decades, their behavior has been modeled assuming random spatial distributions owing to the lack of direct experimental access to their atomic-scale arrangements. Here, using oxygen-doped α-titanium as a model system, we overcome this fundamental limitation by achieving the first three-dimensional visualization, quantitative counting, and sub-[˚]Angstr¨om positioning of individual interstitial oxygen atoms in the bulk, enabled by super-resolution 4D-STEM ptychography with an adaptive prop agator. We find that interstitial oxygen atoms do not distribute randomly; instead, they exhibit correlated occupancy along the [0001] direction, giving rise to nanoscale ordered domains that are not detectable by conventional imaging. This discovery overturns the long-standing paradigm of randomness in interstitial systems and provides a microscopic foundation for understanding anomalous transport, strengthening, and phase stability in interstitial-engineered materials. Our approach establishes a general platform for atomic-scale defect metrology, opening avenues to ratio nally design materials through precise control of interstitial architectures in metals, semiconductors, and quantum solids.

fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. This provides a consistent foundation for simulations, establishing that expansion can serve as a source of counter-propagating waves…

fundamentals.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

fundamentals.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
fundamentals.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.
fundamentals.topic: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

fundamentals.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
fundamentals.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1 , 2 1 / 3 , 2 − 1 / 3 . This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) ( 2 , 2 ) . The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) ( 3 , 3 ) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL ( 2 , Z ) 3 ∖ SL ( 2 , R ) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

fundamentals.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
fundamentals.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point ξ ξ , with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher–Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

fundamentals.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
fundamentals.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” ( physis ) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a helpful point of reference for thinking about how competitive, polarizing speech affects the substantive categories of political debate and analysis, and through them political action.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks. fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive…

fundamentals.title: Constructive Ordinal Exponentiation
fundamentals.abstract: In classical mathematics, ordinal arithmetic is well-studied; constructively, addition and multiplication are well-known. We study constructive ordinal exponentiation, where ordinals are taken to be transitive, extensional, and wellfounded orders on sets. We present a negative result showing that general constructive ordinal exponentiation is impossible, but we suggest two definitions that come close. The first definition is abstract and solely motivated by the expected equations; this works as long as the base of the exponential is positive. The second definition is based on decreasing lists and can be seen as a constructive version of Sierpiński’s definition via functions with finite support; this requires the base to have a trichotomous least element. Whenever it makes sense to ask the question, the two constructions are equivalent, allowing us to prove algebraic laws, cancellation properties, and preservation of decidability of the exponential. The core ideas do not depend on any specific constructive set theory or type theory, but a concrete computer-checked mechanization using the Agda proof assistant is given in homotopy type theory.

fundamentals.title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

fundamentals.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
fundamentals.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax…
